stem: You work for a publisher whose Gemini application summarizes articles for editors. Since last week's deployment, editors have reported recurring style errors despite several prompt revisions. Your BigQuery table contains 1,000 article-and-approved-summary pairs, including 200 examples explicitly marked for evaluation. You want to fine-tune Gemini directly from this table using SQL without exporting the examples, while keeping every marked evaluation example out of training. What should you do?
correct_answer: Create a BigQuery ML remote model over a Gemini model that supports supervised tuning. Supply article prompts and approved summaries through a training query, use a custom split matching the evaluation markers, and evaluate the tuned model.
correct_explanation: The workflow needs supervised tuning through SQL, no data export, and preservation of the designated evaluation set. BigQuery ML can create a tuned Gemini remote model using a query that supplies prompts and target labels. A custom split assigns marked examples to evaluation and the remaining 800 examples to training. Use EVALUATE afterward because tuning does not guarantee improvement. Prompting alone does not tune Gemini, a random split does not preserve the designated evaluation set, and the proposed Agent Platform Studio workflow exports the examples.
distractor_1: Keep the pretrained Gemini remote model in BigQuery ML. Include approved summaries as examples in generation prompts, leave the marked evaluation examples out of those prompts, and evaluate the resulting summaries using the marked examples.
distractor_1_explanation: This fails the requirement to fine-tune Gemini. Providing examples in generation prompts is prompting with a pretrained model. Supervised tuning instead trains on labeled examples and produces a model with learned parameters adapted to the task.
distractor_2: Create a BigQuery ML remote model over a Gemini model that supports supervised tuning. Supply article prompts and approved summaries through a training query, randomly reserve 20% for evaluation, and evaluate the tuned model.
distractor_2_explanation: This fails the requirement to keep every marked evaluation example out of training. BigQuery ML random splitting assigns examples independently of the designated evaluation markers. Reserving the same percentage does not preserve the same examples; a custom split uses the markers to determine membership.
distractor_3: Export the unmarked examples and marked evaluation examples into separate Cloud Storage datasets. Use Agent Platform Studio to tune a supported Gemini model with those training and validation datasets, and evaluate the tuned model.
distractor_3_explanation: This fails the requirement to perform tuning directly from the BigQuery table using SQL without exporting examples. Agent Platform Studio accepts training and validation datasets from Cloud Storage, so this proposed workflow requires an export. BigQuery ML can supply the examples directly through its model-creation query.
